chunks: He (peace be upon him) said: Indeed, Allah, the Exalted, is not a tyrant to His servant, nor unaware of him, nor ignorant of his state, nor heedless of him. Rather, He is All-Knowing, All-Wise. He has counted everything in knowledge, recorded it in a Book, counted it by number, counted it by knowledge, counted it by action, counted it by decree, counted it by wisdom, counted it by judgment, counted it by will, counted it by desire, counted it by power.
ai.seo_question: What attributes of Allah ensure He is not unjust or unaware of His servants?
ai.summary: In *Kamal al-Din*, Shaykh al-Saduq utilizes this narration to reinforce the doctrine of divine justice (*Adl*) against the Mu'tazila and Ahl al-Sunnah, affirming that God’s omnipotence is coupled with perfect wisdom rather than arbitrary will. It underscores that every detail of a servant’s existence is meticulously accounted for, dispelling notions of divine negligence or tyranny. This context is crucial for understanding the Shia view of predestination (*Jabr*) versus free will (*Tafwid*), emphasizing that God’s knowledge encompasses all actions without coercing them.
